sources.label: index.ts listResolvedChanges terminal fan-out
sources.summary: Terminal listing unions memo+visibility+disk+archive IDs then calls getTemporalChange for EVERY candidate in batches of 20. Archive-only IDs (no live workflow) each pay a doomed live Temporal query + classify + reseed path.

sources.label: getTemporalChange archive-only cost
sources.summary: loadDiskTerminalProjection returns only for status 'closed', NOT 'archived'. Archived-only candidates skip the terminal fast path, hit a cache miss, then execute a live changeStateQuery that will fail WorkflowNotFound, then classifyTemporalReadFailure, then reseedChangeFromDisk — 2-3 sequential I/O + Temporal round-trips per archived change.

sources.label: runTemporalQuery per-attempt 5s timeout
sources.summary: Each live query is bounded at 5s. WorkflowNotFound classifies as 'fallback' (retry-wrapper.ts:60-67) so retries short-circuit, but a hung/wedged worker makes each failed candidate query cost up to 5s; classifyTemporalReadFailure can add another describe() up to 5s (shared.ts:250-267,287-293).

sources.label: listSummary terminal defer
sources.summary: Any terminal or content-filtered listSummary call delegates wholesale to listResolvedChanges, so the summary/memo fast path is entirely bypassed for includeArchived. hydrationStats is returned but there is no partial/degraded contract.

sources.label: No degraded-result contract on change listing; reusable warnings primitive exists
sources.summary: adv_change_list has no partial/degraded/warnings envelope. Sibling aggregators (backlog_state/wip_state) already isolate per-source failure into a `warnings[]` array — a proven in-repo pattern to reuse for degraded terminal listing.

sources.label: Temporal maintainer: querying completed workflows replays history; not retained long
sources.summary: antonio.perez + maxim confirm queries against completed workflows force worker history pull+replay unless cached, and Temporal does not retain completed workflows/visibility records long — durable external store (disk/archive bundle) is the recommended read source. Validates reading archive bundle BEFORE attempting a live query for terminal IDs.

sources.label: Temporal Visibility List/Count is the canonical list-by-state path
sources.summary: Visibility List Filter + Count API are the documented cheap path to enumerate/filter/count workflows by ExecutionStatus without per-workflow query, distinct from workflow query which replays history.

sources.label: Existing stale-memo/archive-dominance tests but no bounded-budget/degraded test
sources.summary: Coverage exists for stale memo invalidation and archive-bundle dominance, but there is no test asserting bounded per-candidate cost, no-hard-timeout under large terminal state, or a degraded/partial contract.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Root cause of #106 is a per-candidate live-query fan-out on the terminal listing path. For includeArchived/includeClosed, listResolvedChanges enumerates the FULL union (memo ∪ Visibility ∪ disk ∪ archive) and runs getTemporalChange on each ID sequentially-per-batch (batch=20). Active changes resolve cheaply (cache/query hit), but every archive-only ID follows the expensive miss path: cache miss → live changeStateQuery that WILL fail WorkflowNotFound (Temporal evicts/GCs completed workflows — confirmed by maxim) → classifyTemporalReadFailure (possibly another describe) → reseedChangeFromDisk (disk/archive read). This inverts Temporal's documented guidance: for terminal state the durable external projection (archive bundle / disk) is authoritative and should be read FIRST; the live query is pure waste for archived IDs. loadDiskTerminalProjection already short-circuits 'closed' but NOT 'archived' — a one-line-shaped asymmetry that forces archived changes through the doomed live-query path. Latency scales O(#archived) × (disk + failed-query + classify + reseed); under a wedged worker each failed query burns up to 5s, trivially blowing a 10s tool budget. The active-only path is untouched by any proposed fix because it does not enter the terminal union or the archived miss path.

validation.notes: Leverage points are inside the approved In-Scope aggregate read paths (adv_change_list, adv_status, archive readback, Visibility fallback). No candidate weakens spec-law, archive correctness, gate sequencing, or the active fast path. External Temporal guidance corroborates the archive-first read direction. Design must still pick the exact degraded-result shape and bounded-budget mechanism (user deferred 'degraded_behavior' to design).

tradeoffs: Archive-first fast path for archived IDs eliminates the doomed live query but must preserve stale-projection-vs-terminal-truth correctness already guarded by archive-bundle dominance tests (index.test.ts:1108+).

A bounded per-list budget with a degraded/partial envelope changes the adv_change_list response contract; consumers and tests must tolerate a warnings/partial field (mitigated by reusing the existing rq-backlogCoord04 warnings pattern).
Parallelizing or batching archive-bundle reads reduces latency but raises transient memory/FD pressure on very large archives — batch size stays a tunable.

Skipping the live query for archived IDs slightly narrows self-healing reseed coverage for genuinely-orphaned-but-recoverable workflows; acceptable because archived state is terminal and durable on disk.

alternatives_considered.option: Do nothing / raise the tool timeout
alternatives_considered.rationale: Violates 'no hard timeout in normal large-state conditions' and just defers the cliff; latency still scales with archive count.

alternatives_considered.option: Read durable archive/disk projection first for terminal IDs; only attempt live query for non-terminal candidates
alternatives_considered.rationale: Matches Temporal maintainer guidance (completed workflows replay on query; durable external store is authoritative). Removes the dominant per-archived-ID cost while archive-bundle dominance tests already protect terminal-truth correctness.

alternatives_considered.option: Add a bounded per-list time/candidate budget with an explicit degraded/partial warnings envelope
alternatives_considered.rationale: Directly satisfies the 'explicit degraded/partial warnings, never silent partial' user outcome using the proven in-repo warnings[] aggregator pattern; complements (not replaces) the archive-first fix.

alternatives_considered.option: Full Visibility/memo summary-index read model for terminal statuses (no hydration)
alternatives_considered.rationale: High payoff and aligned with docs/repo-improve-prep summary-index model, but larger surface than #106 needs and overlaps the later status-health/TTL Epic entry; surface as follow-up, not this change.

alternatives_considered.option: Suppress the classifyTemporalReadFailure describe() probe on the list path
alternatives_considered.rationale: Real secondary cost, but subsumed once archived IDs no longer attempt the live query; revisit only if profiling shows residual describe() cost on non-terminal misses.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Adopt two tied primitives for this change: (1) archive-first terminal read — for IDs with an archive bundle (or on-disk terminal status), resolve from the durable projection and skip the live changeStateQuery/classify/reseed chain; extend the existing loadDiskTerminalProjection 'closed' short-circuit to cover 'archived'. (2) bounded degraded-result envelope on listResolvedChanges/adv_change_list reusing the rq-backlogCoord04 warnings[] pattern so a partial terminal read returns explicit degraded warnings instead of a hard ToolExecutionTimeout. Defer the full summary-index terminal read model and status-health TTL to the later Epic entry.

sources.label: index.ts loadDiskTerminalProjection
sources.summary: Terminal disk short-circuit returns ONLY when status === 'closed'. Archived records get no terminal short-circuit, so each archived candidate falls through to live workflow query/reseed — the O(N) fan-out root of the #106 archived-list timeout.

sources.label: index.ts getTemporalChange archive override placement
sources.summary: loadArchiveBundleDominantProjection is consulted only when cached/queried status is non-terminal; the archived candidate still executes a live workflow query (line 583-605) before any archive fallback. Reseed path (617-636) also runs before archive resolution for evicted workflows.

sources.label: index.ts listResolvedChanges batch hydration
sources.summary: Batches of 20 call getTemporalChange per candidate. Archive-bundle override lives only in the CATCH branch (818-844); a slow/hung workflow query on the TRY path is not bypassed and consumes the whole tool call.

sources.label: changes.ts terminal listSummary delegation
sources.summary: Terminal/content filters fully delegate to listResolvedChanges with no per-source degraded metadata. One slow source (visibility, workflow query) consumes the whole call and surfaces as unclassified whole-tool timeout.

sources.label: Shared primitive call sites
sources.summary: status archived-branch hygiene, change recovery, and archive-repair all call store.changes.list({includeArchived:true}) → same listResolvedChanges primitive. A terminal-projection-first + degraded envelope fix benefits all three for free.

sources.label: changes.ts stale-shadow pre-scan pattern (existing, reusable)
sources.summary: Both list paths already implement archive-bundle-dominance pre-scan to invalidate stale non-terminal memo/cache. Proven pattern; extend rather than reinvent for AC3 stale-dominance.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The draft design is correctly targeted and boring in the good sense: it extends existing proven patterns (loadArchiveBundleDominantProjection, archive-bundle-dominance pre-scan, source-isolated warnings) rather than introducing new machinery. The single highest-leverage, low-risk win is extending the terminal disk/archive short-circuit to cover 'archived' the same way loadDiskTerminalProjection already covers 'closed' (index.ts:640-653) — this directly removes the O(N) live-workflow-query fan-out that is the observed #106 root cause, and it makes the fast path match the truth rule the catch-branch override already asserts. The degraded envelope (warnings[]/hydrationStats) is compatible-by-construction (additive fields) and matches existing repo aggregate-read warning patterns. Shared-primitive reach is real and cheap: status-hygiene, change recovery, and archive-repair all route through the same list surface. Deterministic fake-slow-source tests are the correct verification choice given the no-wall-clock-budget decision. No design deviation from canonical Temporal read-model practice: Visibility for live enumeration, durable projection for terminal/completed records that lack a useful query path.

validation.notes: Draft design is architecturally sound and aligned with existing repo patterns. Scout surfaces 4 tie-in leverage candidates; all fit within AC1-AC5 and the deferral boundary (C-constraints, DONT1-4, OOS1-3). No contract compromise, security, or release blocker found.

tradeoffs: Archived terminal short-circuit trades a small amount of freshness (durable archive bundle vs live workflow) for large latency/robustness gains; acceptable because archived records are terminal and archive-bundle-dominance is already the asserted truth rule elsewhere.

Additive degraded envelope (warnings[]/hydrationStats) adds response surface that callers must learn to inspect; mitigated because fields are optional and existing callers ignoring them keep working (AC compatibility requirement).

Routing archive resolution before the workflow query on the terminal path adds one archive-bundle existence check per terminal candidate; negligible vs the workflow query cost it replaces, and already cached per-list-call (archiveBundleCache).

Extending the shared primitive to benefit status-hygiene/recovery widens blast radius of the change slightly; mitigated by deterministic regression tests on the active-list no-regression path (AC2/AC4).

alternatives_considered.rationale: Masks structural O(N) fan-out; moves the failure cliff without fixing root cause. Explicitly forbidden by DONT1 and design D2 rationale.

alternatives_considered.option: Full terminal summary-index read model now
alternatives_considered.rationale: Higher payoff but larger than the #106 slice; agreement DONT/OOS defer broader performance program. Correct to defer per D4.

alternatives_considered.option: Query every terminal workflow first, then fall back to archive
alternatives_considered.rationale: The completed/evicted workflow query path is the observed risk; archive-first inverts the cost correctly for terminal records.

alternatives_considered.option: Per-surface fail-fast instead of warnings[] envelope
alternatives_considered.rationale: warnings[]+hydrationStats preserves partial results and compatibility; fail-fast would drop good rows on one bad source. Envelope is the better default; field names refinable in implementation.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Adopt the draft design as-is. Prioritize the archived terminal short-circuit (extend loadDiskTerminalProjection / route loadArchiveBundleDominantProjection before workflow query on the terminal candidate path) as the primary fix — it is the direct root-cause removal. Reuse the existing archive-bundle-dominance pre-scan for AC3. Wire the additive degraded envelope through listResolvedChanges → terminal listSummary → adv_change_list. Confirm the shared primitive win covers status-hygiene and change/recovery in the same PR (cheap, in-scope per AC5).

# Diagnose archived listing timeout

## Why

ADV archived/terminal listing paths can exceed tool timeouts and may shadow correct terminal state with stale fallback projections. Issue #106 reports a terminal/archived listing timeout with healthy Temporal controls, plus recurrence evidence across aggregate Visibility-backed tools.

## Problem

When aggregate read paths include archived or terminal changes, ADV can exceed the tool budget or return stale fallback-derived state. This damages operator trust in status/listing/archive surfaces, especially when archive finalization succeeds but readback times out or misclassifies workflow/query failure.

## User Outcomes

- Operators can request archived/terminal change listings without hard `ToolExecutionTimeout` in normal large-state conditions.
- Operators get explicit degraded/partial-result warnings when aggregate reads cannot complete within budget.
- Terminal archived/closed truth is not shadowed by stale disk projection or ambiguous recovery fallback.
- Active-only listing remains fast and does not pay terminal-state recovery cost.
- Archive/readback outcomes are explainable when finalization succeeds but aggregate verification is slow.

## Scope

### In Scope

- Diagnose issue #106 using source-backed path analysis and bounded local reproduction where safe.
- Inspect aggregate read paths for `adv_change_list`, `adv_status`, archive readback, and related Temporal Visibility/list fallback behavior.
- Identify why archived/terminal inclusion expands latency or recovery fan-out.
- Define and implement a bounded fix if root cause is local and safe for this change.
- Add regression coverage, performance guard, or degraded-result contract covering terminal/archived listing behavior.
- Preserve active-list fast-path behavior and test it explicitly.

### Out of Scope

- Full Temporal storage architecture rewrite.
- Unrelated worktree cleanup timeout behavior unless the same aggregate-read primitive is touched.
- Broader status health TTL work; later Epic entry.
- OCA-specific behavior and issue #104.
- Unrelated cleanup.

### Must Not

- Do not weaken spec-law, gate sequencing, or archive correctness.
- Do not treat stale disk projection as authoritative over reachable live workflow terminal state without explicit recovery mode.
- Do not hide partial/degraded reads as complete success.
- Do not slow the active-only list path to fix archived/terminal paths.
- Do not add polling loops in normal agent/tool context.

## Discovery Findings

### Current State

- `adv_change_list` uses `changes.listSummary` when available, then paginates after store rows return (`plugin/src/tools/change.ts:388-458`).
- Active/default list uses memo/cache/summary and hydrates only misses (`plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/changes.ts:770-1044`).
- Terminal list (`includeArchived`, `includeClosed`, or terminal status) bypasses warm path and delegates to full `listResolvedChanges` (`plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/changes.ts:777-846`).
- `listResolvedChanges` unions memo, Visibility, active disk, and archive IDs, then hydrates candidates in batches of 20 (`plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/index.ts:683-880`).
- Archive-bundle dominance exists, but the terminal disk short-circuit covers closed projections only, not archived (`plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/index.ts:560-653`).
- Existing tests cover small stale memo/archive dominance cases, not large terminal aggregate degraded behavior.

### Extends

- `docs/repo-improve-prep.md`: prior pack identified full hydration and summary-index opportunity; current discovery narrows the remaining risk to terminal list paths.
- Issue #106: timeout evidence. Current code still has O(N) terminal hydration.
- Issue #198: same fallback/recovery area; full workflow reset remains separate unless a shared helper is touched.
- Issues #53/#57/#88: prior archive/read-state defects; current change adds bounded terminal-list guardrails.

### User Clarifications

- Degraded behavior: defer exact shape to design for Temporal best practice and repo fit.
- Surface scope: cover all easy-medium wins.
- Latency budget: no fixed wall-clock budget; require no hard timeout and clear degradation where appropriate.

### Recommended Objectives

1. Make archived/closed aggregate listing complete or explicitly degraded instead of whole-tool timeout.
2. Ensure archive bundle/durable terminal projection dominates stale active/draft projections in terminal-aware reads.
3. Preserve active-only listing fast path and existing default-list behavior.
4. Add deterministic regression coverage for terminal-list timeout/shadow classes without relying on real wall-clock flakiness.
5. Document and defer broader workflow reset/status TTL/worktree cleanup work unless shared primitive fixes cover them naturally.

### Draft Spec Deltas

- `rq-terminalAggregateRead01`: terminal aggregate reads return complete or structured degraded result, not unclassified whole-tool `ToolExecutionTimeout`, when one terminal source is slow/unavailable/corrupt.
- `rq-terminalProjectionTruth01`: archive bundle truth dominates stale non-terminal projections in terminal-aware reads.
- `rq-activeListFastPath01`: active-only/default list avoids full terminal reconciliation when summary data is sufficient.

### Design Questions

- Terminal degraded response shape: `warnings[]`, `_degraded`, or fail-fast by surface.
- Terminal source priority: archive/disk-first for terminal aggregate candidates versus live-workflow-first.
- Surface breadth: exact shared primitive coverage for `adv_change_list`, status hygiene, and archive readback.
- Budget expression: deterministic slow-source/candidate tests versus real-time latency assertions.

### Discovery Opportunity Scout

Scout report persistence timed out before worker restart, but inline findings were usable. Adopted: archive-first terminal resolution and bounded degraded terminal aggregate envelope. Deferred: full terminal summary-index model. Rejected: raising tool timeout.

### Ambiguity Analysis

No blocking ambiguity. Coverage: B:C F:C S:C M:C. Advisory: exact degraded shape is design-owned.

# Design

## Architecture Overview

Use a terminal-aware aggregate-read path that treats durable terminal projections as the read source for archived/closed records, while preserving the existing active summary fast path.

Core shape:

1. Keep default active/in-flight `adv_change_list` on `changes.listSummary` memo/cache/summary rows.
2. For terminal filters (`includeArchived`, `includeClosed`, `status: "archived"`, `status: "closed"`), enumerate candidate IDs from memo, Visibility, active disk, and archive directories as today.
3. Resolve terminal candidates with durable terminal projection first:
   - archive bundle for archived records;
   - closed disk projection for closed records;
   - only then live workflow query/recovery when no terminal projection exists or status is non-terminal.
4. Return structured degraded aggregate metadata when one candidate/source cannot be resolved within bounded logic, rather than letting one slow source consume the whole tool call.
5. Let shared primitive fixes benefit `adv_change_list`, `change/recovery.ts`, and status archived-hygiene paths that already call the same store listing surface; avoid separate status/worktree rewrites.

## Key Decisions

### D1 — Terminal projection first for terminal aggregate reads

Decision: archived/closed aggregate reads prefer durable terminal projections before live workflow query/reseed.

Rationale:
- Archived workflows may be completed, evicted, or expensive to query/replay.
- Existing `loadDiskTerminalProjection` only short-circuits `closed`; archived should get equivalent terminal short-circuit when an archive bundle/durable projection exists.
- Current archive override can happen after a failed query path; the root-cause fix is to put archive resolution before workflow query for terminal candidates.

### D2 — Structured degraded envelope instead of timeout inflation

Decision: terminal aggregate read APIs return complete rows or explicit degraded metadata naming failed/omitted source classes.

Rationale:
- Raising the tool timeout only moves the failure cliff.
- Existing repo patterns use source-isolated warnings for aggregate reads.
- Partial/degraded output must not masquerade as complete success.

Proposed additive `adv_change_list` response extension:

```ts
{
  changes: ChangeListRow[],
  pagination: Pagination,
  warnings?: Array<{
    code: "TERMINAL_SOURCE_DEGRADED" | "TERMINAL_CANDIDATE_OMITTED";
    source: "visibility" | "active_disk" | "archive" | "workflow_query";
    message: string;
    omittedCount?: number;
  }>,
  hydrationStats?: {
    terminalCandidates: number;
    terminalFromArchive: number;
    terminalFromDisk: number;
    terminalFromWorkflow: number;
    omitted: number;
  }
}
```

Implementation refinement from validator: degraded classification must be structural per-candidate collect-and-classify, not a wall-clock timer. Warning rows should include code, source class, and omitted reason/count.

### D3 — Deterministic slow-source tests over real-time budgets

Decision: verify bounded behavior with fakeable slow/unreachable source tests and candidate-level/call-count assertions, not fixed p95 wall-clock tests.

Rationale:
- User chose no fixed latency budget.
- Wall-clock tests are flaky across hosts and CI.
- The failure mode is structural O(N) fan-out through slow live workflow query/recovery; deterministic tests can prove the fan-out is skipped for terminal projections.

### D4 — Narrow shared primitive wins, defer broader performance program

Decision: implement easy/medium wins on shared terminal-list primitive; defer full terminal summary-index model and status TTL work.

Rationale:
- Agreement asks for all easy-medium wins.
- `changes.listSummary` terminal fallback and `listResolvedChanges` are the primary #106 chokepoints.
- Later Epic entries cover broader status probe TTL and performance structure.

## ADR Drafts

None. Decisions are localized store/tool read-path choices with regression tests and spec anchors; no hard-to-reverse ADR needed.

## Implementation Strategy

1. Add/extend a terminal projection resolver in `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/index.ts`:
   - archive bundle/directory lookup by candidate id;
   - fallback to loaded archive `change.json` canonical id;
   - closed disk projection support retained;
   - stale active projection overridden when archive bundle exists.
2. Route terminal aggregate hydration through this resolver before `getTemporalChange` / live workflow query.
3. Reuse existing archive-bundle pre-scan/dominance pattern from `changes.ts` and `index.ts` instead of adding another heuristic.
4. Add structural candidate/source warning collection for terminal aggregate list failures.
5. Propagate warning/degraded metadata through store listing envelope and `adv_change_list` output without changing existing required fields.
6. Keep default active listing path unchanged except for tests proving it does not enter terminal reconciliation when summary data is sufficient.
7. Add or update specs in `advance-workflow` for terminal aggregate read behavior, projection truth, and active fast-path preservation with concrete rq-* IDs and Given/When/Then scenarios.
8. Add deterministic tests:
   - archived-only candidate with unreachable workflow resolves from archive without workflow query;
   - corrupt/missing terminal candidate creates degraded warning and does not abort unrelated rows;
   - stale active projection + archive bundle returns archived and excludes from default list;
   - active summary path avoids terminal reconciliation and preserves current rows;
   - status archived-hygiene and change recovery callers benefit through same store primitive, or are explicitly unchanged with evidence.

## LBP Analysis

Preferred long-term approach:

- Temporal Visibility remains the right source for enumerating live/open workflows.
- Durable terminal projections are the right read source for terminal/completed records that may no longer have a useful workflow query path.
- Aggregate tools should isolate per-source failures and surface structured degraded metadata instead of depending on global tool timeouts.
- Zod/tool validation and Temporal signal/query correctness stay intact.

Rejected alternatives:

- Raise 10s tool timeout: rejected; masks structural fan-out.
- Query every terminal workflow first: rejected; replays/completed workflow query path is the observed risk.
- Full terminal summary-index model now: deferred; higher payoff but larger than this change.

## Affected Components

- `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/index.ts` — terminal projection resolution and `listResolvedChanges` hydration order.
- `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/changes.ts` — terminal `listSummary` fallback metadata propagation and existing archive pre-scan reuse.
- `plugin/src/storage/store-types.ts` — listing envelope type if warning metadata needs a typed store shape.
- `plugin/src/tools/change.ts` — `adv_change_list` response metadata pass-through.
- `plugin/src/tools/status-hygiene.ts` and `plugin/src/tools/change/recovery.ts` — no standalone rewrite expected; verify they benefit or remain safe through shared `store.changes.list` primitive.
- `.adv/specs/advance-workflow/spec.json` and docs mirror if spec deltas are implemented.
- Tests under `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/*test.ts` and `plugin/src/tools/change*.test.ts` as needed.

## Design-Derived Criteria

DDC1: Terminal aggregate hydration must not call live workflow query for archived candidates when a matching archive bundle/durable archived projection exists.

DDC2: Degraded terminal aggregate output must include machine-readable warning code, source class, and omitted count or reason.

DDC3: Active/default `listSummary` with memo/cache summary data must remain terminal-reconciliation-free.

DDC4: Archive bundle dominance must dedupe by canonical `change.json.id`, not directory name.

DDC5: Tests must use injected fake/slow source behavior or call-count assertions instead of wall-clock latency thresholds.

DDC6: Shared-primitive callers (`status-hygiene`, `change/recovery`) must be covered by tests or explicit source evidence when terminal-list behavior changes.

## Risks / Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Partial degraded rows mistaken as complete | Explicit warning metadata; AC requires source/omitted class naming. |
| Archive-first hides recoverable active workflow | Use archive-first only in terminal-aware reads when archive/durable terminal projection exists. |
| Response contract drift breaks callers | Add optional metadata only; preserve `changes` and `pagination` fields. |
| Corrupt archive bundle crashes list | Catch per-candidate/source failure; record warning; continue unrelated rows. |
| Broader status/worktree scope creep | Restrict to shared primitive and explicitly defer non-shared status TTL/worktree cleanup. |

## Design Leverage Scout

Validator scout result: pass, high confidence, low risk.

Auto-adopted:
- Extend terminal short-circuit to `archived` and reorder archive-before-query in `index.ts` root path.
- Add source-isolated degraded envelope at terminal list boundary.
- Reuse existing archive-bundle pre-scan/dominance pattern for stale-shadow correctness.

Surfaced and incorporated within existing agreement:
- Confirm shared primitive coverage for `status-hygiene.ts` and `change/recovery.ts`; direct edits only if tests show metadata handling requires it.

Deferred:
- Full terminal summary-index model.

## Validator Result

Validator: clean pass.

- Correctness: pass. Root cause verified as query-first per terminal candidate; design reorders terminal projection before query and adds degraded metadata.
- Simplicity: pass. Narrow shared primitive is simpler than full summary-index model and avoids timeout inflation.
- Spec-law: pass. Design strengthens archive terminal projection behavior and replay fallback semantics; implementation must add concrete `advance-workflow` rq-* deltas before code tasks.
- Key alternatives considered: timeout inflation rejected; summary-index deferred; per-source fail-fast rejected; status quo rejected.

Non-blocking validator refinement adopted: mechanize degraded classification structurally per candidate, not with wall-clock timers.
